name: 15-day format test (owner decision Oct 26, 2026)
rule: Two Reels a day at 12:00 and 18:00 (America/Guatemala), BOTH in that day's format, different subject/product. Same narrator family, same end card and CTA (Your first ad is on us. DM 'DAILY') on every video, so only the format changes. No faces of the owner, no real client work (owner said no).
metrics: Rank on lifetime numbers at the end: (1) watch % = avg watch time / length, (2) shares+saves per 100 reached, (3) follows + 'DAILY' DMs. Raw views are reported but not used to rank (small account, distribution is noisy and grows over time).
final_report: 2026-11-11 ~12:30 PM: re-pull all lifetime insights, rank formats, recommend the 2–3 to keep; pause new posting on Nov 11 until the owner decides.

formats.name: Tension
formats.how: Something is about to happen (pin→balloon). Silent 4 s hook, a fake-out mid-way, narrator names the feeling, pitch, payoff at the very end. Engine: engine/retention/pin_*.py.

formats.name: Before / After
formats.how: A boring, typical product ad (flat, generic, stock-y) plays first and is labelled BEFORE; then our version of the same product, labelled AFTER. Narrator: 'Same product. Different ad.' Pitch + CTA.

formats.name: Text order → finished ad
formats.how: A client-style text message arrives ('can you make an ad for my ___?'), quick process glimpses (script, footage, edit), then the finished mini-ad. Honest: no fake clock times, 'example order'.

formats.name: Narrated showcase
formats.how: 'Here's how we'd sell your ___' — narrator over a plain shot, then a cinematic ~10 s mini-ad with its own music, then 'your logo here', CTA. Engine: _system/engine/promo/.

formats.name: Satisfying close-ups, no voice
formats.how: No narration. Macro product shots cut to a beat (pour, crunch, unbox, spin), bold on-screen text tells the story ('This is how a product should feel'). Text CTA at the end + music sting.

formats.name: POV text story
formats.how: 'POV: your café's Reels finally get views' — first-person text-on-screen story over footage (posting into the void → we take over → people stop scrolling). Light narration or none.

formats.name: List
formats.how: '3 reasons people skip your ads' — numbered, fast, each reason shown visually with a bad example, then the fix (us). Narrated.

formats.name: Hot take
formats.how: Bold opener on screen + voice: 'Your product isn't boring. Your ad is.' Argue it in 3 beats with visual proof, then the offer.

formats.name: Pattern interrupt
formats.how: Opens as something else entirely (a fake 'video buffering' glitch, a weather report, a cooking clip) and twists into the pitch at ~3 s: 'Got you. That's what a hook does.'

formats.name: Guess the product
formats.how: Extreme close-ups / abstract shots, on-screen 'Guess the product' with a counter; reveal at the end; narrator: 'You watched to find out. Your customers would too.'

formats.name: Mini skit
formats.how: A thumb scrolls a fake feed past 4 dull ads (quick, muted), then stops dead on ours; the ad plays. Narrator: 'That's the one they stop for.' Built with phone mockups, no faces needed.

formats.name: Proof chart
formats.how: Animated retention graph: a typical ad's viewers dropping off a cliff in 2 s vs a curve that holds — built from a narrated, honest explanation of how retention works (no fake client numbers; label as illustration).

formats.name: Useful tip
formats.how: Pure value: 'One trick to keep people watching your ad' (open a loop in the first second and close it at the end), demonstrated live in the video itself. Save-worthy. Soft CTA.

formats.name: Seamless loop
formats.how: A short (8–12 s) piece whose last frame flows perfectly into the first, so it auto-replays; text + a line of voice. Measures whether loops inflate watch time.

formats.name: Direct offer
formats.how: Blunt and plain: 'Free ad. What's the catch? There isn't one.' Shows example work fast, explains exactly how to claim it (DM DAILY, tell us your product), what happens next.

posts.note: second Tension Reel (day 1 only had one), different object, so every format has two
